title: ICSE CLASS 10 — Chemistry | Periodic Classification Elements
description: Subject-wise test on Periodic Classification Elements (Chemistry) for ICSE CLASS 10. 50Q.
subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: The Modern Periodic Law states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their:

options.explanation: Atomic mass is not the correct basis for the Modern Periodic Law.
Atomic volume is not the correct basis for the Modern Periodic Law.
The Modern Periodic Law is based on the atomic number.
Electronic configuration is related to the atomic number but is not the direct basis for the Modern Periodic Law.

questions.explanation: The Modern Periodic Law, proposed by Moseley, is based on the atomic number, which is a more fundamental property than atomic mass and provides a better classification of elements.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: An element has an atomic number of 17. To which group and period does it belong?

options.explanation: The element with atomic number 17 is not in Period 2.
The element with atomic number 17 is in Period 3 and Group 17.
Group 7 is an old notation; the correct notation for this group is Group 17.
The element with atomic number 17 is not in Period 2 or Group 7 in the modern notation.

questions.explanation: The electronic configuration of an element with atomic number 17 is 2, 8, 7. The number of shells (3) determines the period, so it is in Period 3. The number of valence electrons (7) indicates it belongs to Group 17 (or VIIA, as 10 + 7 = 17 for p-block elements).
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the metallic character of elements down a group in the periodic table?

options.explanation: Metallic character increases down a group.
Metallic character increases down a group due to increased atomic size and decreased nuclear attraction on outer electrons.
Metallic character does not remain constant down a group.
There is no decrease in metallic character down a group in the periodic table.

questions.explanation: Down a group, the atomic size increases due to the addition of new shells, and the nuclear attraction on the outermost electrons decreases. This makes it easier for atoms to lose electrons, thereby increasing their metallic character.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: An element 'X' belongs to Group 1 of the periodic table. Which of the following is most likely to be its characteristic?

options.explanation: Group 1 elements form basic oxides, not acidic oxides.
Group 1 elements are alkali metals, not noble gases.

options.text: It readily loses one electron to form a positive ion.
options.explanation: Group 1 elements readily lose one electron to form a positive ion.
Group 1 elements have low electronegativity.

questions.explanation: Elements in Group 1 are alkali metals. They have one valence electron, which they readily lose to achieve a stable duplet or octet configuration, forming a unipositive ion (e.g., Na+). They form basic oxides and have low electronegativity.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Arrange the following elements in decreasing order of their atomic size: Na, Mg, Al, Si

options.explanation: This order is incorrect as it suggests Si is larger than the others, which contradicts the trend across a period.
This order does not correctly reflect the decreasing atomic size across the period from left to right.
This is the correct order of decreasing atomic size across Period 3 from left to right.
This order is incorrect as Mg is to the right of Na in the periodic table and should have a smaller atomic size.

questions.explanation: Na, Mg, Al, and Si belong to the same period (Period 3). Across a period from left to right, the atomic number and nuclear charge increase, while the number of shells remains the same. This leads to a stronger pull on the valence electrons, causing the atomic size to decrease. Therefore, Na has the largest size, and Si has the smallest.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following elements has the highest ionization energy?

options.explanation: K has a lower ionization energy than Li due to its larger size and weaker nuclear attraction on the valence electron.
Na has a lower ionization energy than Li for the same reasons as K.
Li has the highest ionization energy among the given options due to its small size and strong nuclear attraction on its valence electron.
Cs has the lowest ionization energy among the given options due to its large size and weak nuclear attraction on its valence electron.

questions.explanation: Ionization energy generally decreases down a group. This is because atomic size increases, and the outermost electron is further from the nucleus and experiences greater shielding, making it easier to remove. Among Li, Na, K, and Cs (all Group 1 elements), Lithium is at the top of the group and thus has the smallest atomic size and the strongest nuclear attraction on its valence electron, requiring the most energy to remove it.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Electronegativity generally increases across a period from left to right because:

options.text: Atomic size increases and nuclear charge decreases.
options.explanation: This is the opposite of what happens across a period.

options.text: Atomic size remains constant and nuclear charge decreases.
options.explanation: Both atomic size and nuclear charge do not remain constant across a period.

options.text: Atomic size decreases and nuclear charge increases.
options.explanation: This is the correct relationship across a period, leading to increased electronegativity.

options.text: Atomic size increases and nuclear charge increases.
options.explanation: While nuclear charge increases across a period, atomic size decreases, not increases.

questions.explanation: Across a period, the atomic number and nuclear charge increase, while the number of electron shells remains the same. This results in a stronger effective nuclear charge pulling the valence electrons closer, leading to a decrease in atomic size. A smaller atomic size and stronger nuclear pull increase the tendency of an atom to attract shared electrons, hence increasing electronegativity.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Identify the most reactive non-metal among the following:

options.explanation: While chlorine is reactive, it is not as reactive as fluorine due to its lower electronegativity.
Bromine is less reactive than chlorine and fluorine due to its lower electronegativity and larger size.
Iodine is the least reactive among the given halogens due to its large size and low electronegativity.
Fluorine is the most reactive non-metal among the given options due to its high electronegativity and small size.

questions.explanation: Reactivity of non-metals is related to their tendency to gain electrons (electronegativity and electron affinity). Non-metallic character and reactivity increase across a period and decrease down a group. Fluorine is at the top of Group 17 (halogens) and is the most electronegative element, meaning it has the strongest tendency to gain electrons. Therefore, it is the most reactive non-metal.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Assertion (A): The atomic radius of oxygen is smaller than that of nitrogen. Reason (R): Across a period, the effective nuclear charge increases, pulling the electrons closer to the nucleus.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: While both A and R are true, R does not directly explain why oxygen's atomic radius is smaller than nitrogen's.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: This is correct because R explains the general trend but not the specific comparison between oxygen and nitrogen.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true: Oxygen has a smaller atomic radius than nitrogen. Reason (R) is true: Across a period, the effective nuclear charge increases, pulling the electrons closer to the nucleus, which leads to a decrease in atomic size. However, R is not the correct explanation for A in a direct sense of "why oxygen is smaller than nitrogen." R explains the trend of decreasing atomic radius across a period, which results in oxygen being smaller than nitrogen.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Consider three elements P, Q, and R with atomic numbers 6, 8, and 19 respectively. Which element is a metal, and which is a non-metal with the highest electronegativity among the three?

options.text: P is metal, Q is non-metal with highest electronegativity.
options.explanation: P is not a metal; it is a non-metal (Carbon).

options.text: R is metal, Q is non-metal with highest electronegativity.
options.explanation: R is indeed a metal (Potassium), and Q (Oxygen) is the non-metal with the highest electronegativity among the three.

options.text: Q is metal, P is non-metal with highest electronegativity.
options.explanation: Q is not a metal; it is a non-metal (Oxygen), and P (Carbon) does not have the highest electronegativity among the three.

options.text: R is metal, P is non-metal with highest electronegativity.
options.explanation: While R is correctly identified as a metal, P (Carbon) does not have the highest electronegativity; Q (Oxygen) does.

questions.explanation: Element P (Atomic No. 6): Electronic configuration is 2, 4. It belongs to Period 2, Group 14. It is Carbon, a non-metal. Element Q (Atomic No. 8): Electronic configuration is 2, 6. It belongs to Period 2, Group 16. It is Oxygen, a non-metal. Element R (Atomic No. 19): Electronic configuration is 2, 8, 8, 1. It belongs to Period 4, Group 1. It is Potassium, an alkali metal. Therefore, R is a metal. P and Q are non-metals. Among P (Carbon) and Q (Oxygen), both are in Period 2. Electronegativity increases across a period. Oxygen (Group 16) is to the right of Carbon (Group 14). Thus, Oxygen (Q) has higher electronegativity than Carbon (P). Comparing Q with R, Q is a non-metal with high electronegativity, while R is a metal with very low electronegativity. So, Q is the non-metal with the highest electronegativity among the three.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: The Modern Periodic Table is based on which fundamental property of elements?

options.explanation: Atomic mass is not the fundamental property used in the Modern Periodic Table.
Atomic volume is not a property used to classify elements in the Modern Periodic Table.
The Modern Periodic Table is based on the atomic number of elements.
The number of neutrons is not used as a fundamental property for classifying elements in the Modern Periodic Table.

questions.explanation: Henry Moseley showed that atomic number is a more fundamental property than atomic mass for classifying elements, leading to the Modern Periodic Law.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about elements in the same period of the modern periodic table?

options.text: They have the same number of valence electrons.
options.explanation: Valence electrons vary across a period.
Chemical properties vary across a period.

options.text: They have the same number of electron shells.
options.explanation: Same principal energy level means same number of electron shells.
Atomic masses generally increase across a period but are not similar.

questions.explanation: Elements in the same period have their outermost electrons in the same principal energy level, meaning they have the same number of electron shells. The number of valence electrons and chemical properties vary across a period.
questions.hint: Consider the arrangement of electrons in the same principal energy level.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: As we move down a group in the modern periodic table, the atomic size of elements generally:

options.explanation: New electron shells increase atomic size.
Atomic size increases down a group.
Atomic size changes down a group.
Atomic size consistently increases down a group.

questions.explanation: As we move down a group, a new electron shell is added with each successive element. This increases the distance of the outermost electrons from the nucleus, leading to an increase in atomic size.
questions.hint: Think about the addition of electron shells down a group.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: An element belongs to Group 13 of the modern periodic table. What is its valency?

options.explanation: Valency for Group 13 is 3.
Valency for Group 13 is 3.
Valency for Group 13 is 3.
Valency for Group 13 is 3.

questions.explanation: For main group elements (Groups 13-17), the valency can be calculated as (Group Number - 10) or (18 - Group Number). For Group 13, valency = 13 - 10 = 3.
questions.hint: Use the formula for valency in main group elements.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following elements has the highest electronegativity?

options.explanation: Lithium is less electronegative than Fluorine.
Boron is less electronegative than Fluorine.
Nitrogen is less electronegative than Fluorine.
Fluorine is the most electronegative element.

questions.explanation: Electronegativity generally increases across a period and decreases down a group. Fluorine (F) is located in Period 2, Group 17, and is the most electronegative element in the entire periodic table.
questions.hint: Consider the trend of electronegativity in the periodic table.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Ionization energy generally increases across a period because:

options.text: The number of electron shells increases.
options.explanation: Number of electron shells remains constant across a period.

options.text: The effective nuclear charge increases, and atomic size decreases.
options.explanation: Increased nuclear charge and decreased atomic size increase ionization energy.
Shielding effect does not increase significantly across a period.
Metallic character decreases across a period.

questions.explanation: Across a period, the number of electron shells remains constant, but the nuclear charge increases. This increased nuclear charge pulls the outermost electrons more strongly towards the nucleus, decreasing the atomic size and requiring more energy (ionization energy) to remove an electron.
questions.hint: Consider the effect of increasing nuclear charge on electron removal.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following properties is characteristic of alkali metals (Group 1 elements)?

options.explanation: Alkali metals form basic oxides.
Alkali metals have low ionization energies.
Alkali metals are highly reactive metals.

options.text: They are soft metals with low melting points.
options.explanation: Alkali metals are soft and have low melting points.

questions.explanation: Alkali metals are highly reactive metals with low ionization energies. They typically form basic oxides. They are known for their softness and relatively low melting points due to the presence of only one valence electron leading to weaker metallic bonding.
questions.hint: Consider the properties of Group 1 elements.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Assertion (A): Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties. Reason (R): Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both assertion and reason are true, and the reason explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Both assertion and reason are true.

questions.explanation: Chemical properties of elements are primarily determined by the number of valence electrons. Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons, which leads to them exhibiting similar chemical behavior. Thus, both assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.hint: Consider the role of valence electrons in determining chemical properties.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: An element 'X' has atomic number 17. Which of the following statements about element 'X' is INCORRECT?

options.explanation: Chlorine is a halogen (Group 17).
Chlorine has a valency of 1.
Chlorine forms acidic oxides, not basic.
Chlorine is a non-metal.

questions.explanation: An element with atomic number 17 is Chlorine (Cl). Chlorine is a non-metal and forms acidic oxides (e.g., Cl2O7). Basic oxides are formed by metals. Therefore, the incorrect statement is that it forms a basic oxide.
questions.hint: Identify the element with atomic number 17 and analyze its properties.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Elements with electron configurations ending in s$^1$ or s$^2$ (excluding Helium) are generally found in which block of the periodic table?

options.explanation: Elements ending in s$^1$ or s$^2$ are in the s-block.
p-block elements end in p orbitals.
d-block elements end in d orbitals.
f-block elements end in f orbitals.

questions.explanation: The s-block elements are those in which the last electron enters the s-orbital. These include Group 1 (alkali metals) with s$^1$ configuration and Group 2 (alkaline earth metals) with s$^2$ configuration.
questions.hint: Consider the electron configuration of elements in the s-block.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Consider three elements P, Q, and R from the same period of the periodic table. Their atomic numbers are consecutive, with P having the smallest atomic number. Element R is a noble gas. Which of the following statements is correct regarding these elements?

options.text: Element P has the highest ionization energy among the three.
options.explanation: Ionization energy increases across a period, so R (noble gas) has the highest.
Q is in Group 17 (halogens), which are non-metals.

options.text: Element R has the largest atomic size among the three.
options.explanation: Atomic size decreases across a period, so P has the largest size.

options.text: Element P is likely to be a non-metal.
options.explanation: P is in Group 16, which consists of non-metals.

questions.explanation: Since P, Q, and R are in the same period with consecutive atomic numbers, and R is a noble gas (Group 18), then Q must be in Group 17 (halogens) and P must be in Group 16 (chalcogens). Element P (Group 16) is a non-metal.
questions.hint: Identify the groups of P, Q, and R based on their atomic numbers and the fact that R is a noble gas.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following elements belongs to the Halogen family?

options.explanation: Sodium belongs to Group 1 (Alkali metals).
Chlorine is a member of Group 17 (Halogens).
Calcium belongs to Group 2 (Alkaline earth metals).
Iron is a transition metal.

questions.explanation: Chlorine is a member of Group 17 (Halogens) in the periodic table, characterized by having 7 valence electrons.
questions.hint: Group 17 elements are known as halogens.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: The modern periodic table is based on the arrangement of elements in increasing order of:

options.explanation: The modern periodic table is not based on atomic mass.
The modern periodic table is based on atomic number.
Number of neutrons does not determine the arrangement in the periodic table.
Number of isotopes is not used for arranging elements in the periodic table.

questions.explanation: The modern periodic table follows the modern periodic law, which states that properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about the position of metals, non-metals, and metalloids in the periodic table?

options.text: Metalloids are only found in Group 18

questions.question: Which of the following elements will have the highest electronegativity?

options.explanation: Lithium has low electronegativity.
Beryllium has moderate electronegativity.
Fluorine is the most electronegative element.
Neon is a noble gas and does not form bonds to exhibit electronegativity.

questions.explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element in the periodic table due to its small atomic size and high nuclear charge, making it easier to attract shared electrons.
questions.hint: Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group.

questions.question: In a laboratory, a student observes the following properties of an element: It is a good conductor of heat and electricity. It has a high melting and boiling point. It forms basic oxides. Which of the following could be the element?

options.explanation: Carbon is a non-metal and does not form basic oxides.
Nitrogen is a non-metal and does not form basic oxides.
Iron is a metal with the given properties.
Sulfur is a non-metal and forms acidic oxides.

questions.explanation: Iron is a metal with high melting and boiling points, good electrical and thermal conductivity, and forms basic oxides like FeO and Fe2O3.
questions.hint: Consider the properties of metals.

questions.question: Which of the following elements has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 3?

options.explanation: Magnesium has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 2.
Sodium has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 1.
Aluminium has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 3.
Boron has the electronic configuration 2, 3.

questions.explanation: The electronic configuration 2, 8, 3 corresponds to Aluminium (atomic number 13), with electrons filled in K, L, and M shells respectively.
questions.hint: The sum of the electrons in the configuration is the atomic number.

questions.question: Among the elements Na, Mg, Al, and Si, which has the highest ionization enthalpy?

options.explanation: Silicon has the highest ionization enthalpy among the given elements.
Aluminium has lower ionization enthalpy than silicon.
Magnesium has lower ionization enthalpy than silicon.
Sodium has the lowest ionization enthalpy among the given elements.

questions.explanation: Ionization enthalpy increases across a period due to increasing nuclear charge. Silicon (Si) has a higher ionization enthalpy than Na, Mg, and Al because it has a smaller atomic size and more protons.
questions.hint: Ionization enthalpy generally increases across a period.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of noble gases?

options.explanation: This is a characteristic of noble gases.
Noble gases do not form compounds easily.

options.explanation: This is a characteristic of noble gases.

questions.explanation: Noble gases are chemically inert and rarely form compounds due to their stable electronic configuration. They can form compounds under specific conditions (e.g., XeF2), but this is not a characteristic.
questions.hint: Noble gases are known for their inertness.

questions.question: An element X has atomic number 16. What will be the formula of its hydride?

Sulfur forms the hydride H2S (XH2).
This is not the correct formula for the hydride of sulfur.
This is not the correct formula for the hydride of sulfur.

questions.explanation: Element X with atomic number 16 is sulfur (S), which belongs to Group 16. It forms a hydride with the formula H2S (XH2), as it requires two hydrogen atoms to complete its octet.
questions.hint: Group 16 elements form hydrides with the formula XH2.

Atomic number is the fundamental property that determines the periodic properties of elements.

Chlorine is less electronegative than fluorine.

Iodine is the least electronegative among the given options.

questions.question: Which of the following oxides is acidic in nature?

MgO is a basic oxide as it is formed by a metal.
Al₂O₃ is an amphoteric oxide, meaning it can react as both an acid and a base.
SO₂ is an acidic oxide as it is formed by a non-metal.

questions.explanation: Non-metallic oxides are generally acidic, while metallic oxides are basic. SO₂ is an acidic oxide as it is an oxide of a non-metal.

questions.question: Three elements P, Q, and R are in the 3rd period of the Modern Periodic Table. Their atomic numbers are 11, 13, and 16 respectively. Based on this information, which of the following is correct?

P (Sodium) is a metal and forms a basic oxide.

questions.question: **Assertion (A):** Chlorine has a higher electron affinity than Fluorine. **Reason (R):** Though Fluorine is more electronegative, Chlorine has a larger atomic size allowing for less electron-electron repulsion in its 3p subshell when an electron is added, compared to Fluorine's smaller 2p subshell.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion. Chlorine has a higher electron affinity than Fluorine due to less electron-electron repulsion in its larger 3p subshell.
questions.hint: Electron affinity is the energy released when an electron is added to a neutral atom.

questions.question: The Modern Periodic Law states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their:

options.explanation: Atomic mass was used in the earlier periodic law but not in the Modern Periodic Law.
Atomic volume is not the basis of the Modern Periodic Law.
The Modern Periodic Law is based on the atomic number of elements.
Electronic configuration is a consequence of the atomic number but not the direct basis of the Modern Periodic Law.

questions.explanation: The Modern Periodic Law, proposed by Moseley, is based on the atomic number of elements, which is a more fundamental property than atomic mass.
questions.hint: This law was revised to use a more fundamental property than atomic mass.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: As we move down a group in the Modern Periodic Table, the atomic size of elements generally:

options.explanation: New electron shells increase the atomic size.
Atomic size does not decrease down a group.
Atomic size changes down a group.
Atomic size consistently increases down a group.

questions.explanation: As we move down a group, new electron shells are added to the atoms, increasing the distance of the outermost electrons from the nucleus, thus increasing the atomic size.
questions.hint: Consider the addition of electron shells as you move down a group.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Elements in Group 17 (Halogens) of the Modern Periodic Table typically exhibit which valency?

options.explanation: Halogens gain one electron to achieve a stable octet.
Group 17 elements do not typically exhibit a valency of 2.
Group 17 elements do not typically exhibit a valency of 3.
Valency refers to the combining capacity, not the number of valence electrons.

questions.explanation: Group 17 elements have 7 valence electrons. To achieve a stable octet, they tend to gain one electron, resulting in a valency of 1.
questions.hint: Group 17 elements need one more electron to complete their octet.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following elements has the highest metallic character?

options.explanation: Sodium is in Group 1 but is above Potassium in the periodic table.
Magnesium is in Group 2, which has lower metallic character than Group 1.
Potassium is in Group 1, Period 4, making it the most metallic among the given options.
Calcium is in Group 2, which has lower metallic character than Group 1.

questions.explanation: Metallic character increases down a group and decreases across a period. Potassium (K) is in Group 1, Period 4, while Sodium (Na) is in Group 1, Period 3. Both Magnesium (Mg) and Calcium (Ca) are in Group 2. Therefore, Potassium (K) is more metallic than Sodium (Na), and both K and Na are more metallic than Mg and Ca because they are in Group 1. Hence, Potassium (K) has the highest metallic character among the given options.
questions.hint: Metallic character increases down a group and decreases across a period.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: An element has an electronic configuration of 2, 8, 7. To which group and period of the Modern Periodic Table does it belong?

options.explanation: The element has 3 electron shells (Period 3) and 7 valence electrons (Group 17).
Group 7 does not exist in the Modern Periodic Table; Group 17 is the correct group for 7 valence electrons.
The element has 3 electron shells, so it is in Period 3, not Period 2.
Group 7 does not exist, and the element has 3 electron shells, so it is in Period 3.

questions.explanation: The number of shells (3 in this case: 2, 8, 7) indicates the period number, so it's Period 3. The number of valence electrons (7 in this case) indicates the group number (for p-block elements, it's 10 + valence electrons). So, it belongs to Group 17 (10 + 7).
questions.hint: Count the number of electron shells for the period and the valence electrons for the group.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Among the following elements belonging to the third period, which one forms an amphoteric oxide?

options.explanation: Sodium forms a strongly basic oxide (Na₂O).
Magnesium forms a basic oxide (MgO).
Aluminium forms an amphoteric oxide (Al₂O₃).
Phosphorus forms an acidic oxide (P₂O₅).

questions.explanation: Across the third period, the nature of oxides changes from basic to amphoteric to acidic. Sodium (Na) forms a strongly basic oxide (Na₂O), Magnesium (Mg) forms a basic oxide (MgO), Aluminium (Al) forms an amphoteric oxide (Al₂O₃), and Phosphorus (P) forms an acidic oxide (P₂O₅).
questions.hint: Amphoteric oxides can react with both acids and bases.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Ionization energy generally decreases down a group. Reason (R): The atomic size increases down a group, and the outermost electrons are farther from the nucleus, experiencing less nuclear attraction.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both A and R are correct, and R correctly explains A.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: R is the correct explanation of A.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: A is true.

questions.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are correct. As atomic size increases down a group, the outermost electrons are further from the positively charged nucleus, and there is increased shielding effect from inner electrons. Both these factors reduce the effective nuclear charge experienced by the valence electrons, making it easier to remove them, hence decreasing the ionization energy. Therefore, R correctly explains A.
questions.hint: Consider the relationship between atomic size, nuclear attraction, and ionization energy.

questions.question: Three elements X, Y, and Z have atomic numbers 11, 12, and 17 respectively. Based on their positions in the periodic table, choose the correct statement:

options.text: X is a non-metal, Y is a metalloid, Z is a metal.
options.explanation: X and Y are metals, Z is a non-metal.

options.text: X has higher electronegativity than Y.
options.explanation: Y has higher electronegativity than X.

options.text: Y has a larger atomic size than X.
options.explanation: X has a larger atomic size than Y.

options.text: Z has a higher electron affinity than X.
options.explanation: Z (Chlorine) has a higher electron affinity than X (Sodium).

questions.explanation: Element X (atomic number 11) is Sodium (Na) - Group 1, Period 3 (Metal). Element Y (atomic number 12) is Magnesium (Mg) - Group 2, Period 3 (Metal). Element Z (atomic number 17) is Chlorine (Cl) - Group 17, Period 3 (Non-metal). Evaluating the options: A) Incorrect (X and Y are metals, Z is a non-metal). B) Incorrect (Y has higher electronegativity than X). C) Incorrect (X has a larger atomic size than Y). D) Correct (Z has a higher electron affinity than X).
questions.hint: Identify the elements and their positions in the periodic table before evaluating the options.

questions.question: The tendency of an atom to attract a shared pair of electrons towards itself in a chemical bond is called:

options.explanation: Ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron.
Electron affinity is the energy released when an electron is added.
Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom to attract a shared pair of electrons.
Metallic character relates to the tendency to lose electrons.

questions.explanation: Electronegativity is the measure of the tendency of an atom to attract a bonding pair of electrons. Ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron, and electron affinity is the energy released when an electron is added. Metallic character relates to the tendency to lose electrons.
questions.hint: This property is related to the attraction of electrons in a chemical bond.
